title: Canada Promises $560 Million to Help Protect Rainforests
summary:
Canada has promised up to $560 million over four years to help protect rainforests around the world. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the promise on Sunday in Manila during a meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva at an ASEAN summit.

The money will go to the Tropical Forests Forever Facility, a fund led by Brazil and Norway. The fund was launched at the COP30 climate summit in Brazil last year. It aims to grow to $125 billion, with about $100 billion coming from private-sector investors. It would help protect more than one billion hectares of tropical forest each year in more than 70 countries. Countries would be paid for verified results, and at least 20 percent would go to Indigenous people and local communities.

The promise is part of a $6-billion fund Canada promised this spring for international climate finance, and part of Canada's bigger promise to provide more than $13 billion in climate finance to developing countries by 2031. Carney said protecting tropical forests helps slow biodiversity loss, steady the climate, and protect communities.
why_it_matters: Rainforests help keep the air clean and the climate steady, which matters for the world kids will grow up in.

keywords.explanation: Indigenous people are the first people who lived in a place, long before others arrived.
Biodiversity means the many different kinds of plants and animals that live in a place.
A hectare is a way to measure a large area of land.
Verified means checked and shown to be true.
A summit is a big meeting of leaders from different countries.
Investors are people or groups that put money into something to help it grow.

background_read: Rainforests are thick forests in warm, wet parts of the world that are home to many plants and animals, and they help keep the air and climate steady.
When rainforests are cut down, the plants and animals that live there lose their homes, and the climate can change.
Countries sometimes put money into a shared fund to pay other countries to keep their forests standing.
